edges.effect_quant: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.population: infants with risk of iron deficiency
edges.mechanism: This early-life or prenatal exposure may shape Childhood neurodevelopment through developmental programming, microbiome establishment, immune maturation, or nutrient sufficiency during sensitive windows. Timing matters because the same exposure can be much more consequential in infancy or pregnancy than later in life.
edges.summary: In infants with risk of iron deficiency, dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts suggest that iron supplementation in infancy tracks with favorable shifts in childhood neurodevelopment. Most disagreement in the literature is about size, subgroup sensitivity, or dose threshold rather than about whether the relationship exists at all.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
